rules.summary: A component responsibility uses a vague qualifier with no concrete metric. Demoted to info when the sentence carries a number.
Two actions joined by a conjunction in one responsibility — the component is doing two jobs.
An error mode gestures at failure rather than naming one.
The contract is provided but consumed by no component. Set-level check: not decidable from a single file.
Consequences list only upsides; no cost is recorded. A decision with no downside was not a decision.
A decision driver names no threshold the chosen option can be checked against. Demoted to info when the line carries a number.
An option listed in frontmatter never appears under the 'Considered Options' heading, so it was named but not weighed.
A cycle in the component graph where every individual edge resolves. Set-level check: invisible one file at a time.
A vague qualifier with no concrete metric. Demoted to info when the sentence carries a number.
Multiple actions joined by a conjunction in one requirement, which cannot be verified or traced as a single unit.
The description does not match the shape of the EARS pattern the requirement declares.
Passive voice hides the responsible actor.
An implementation detail appears in a requirement whose tier should stay solution-free.
A glossary term no requirement uses. Set-level check: not decidable from a single file.
A design artifact's traces_from names a requirement ID that does not exist in the requirements set.
A requirement ID listed under '## Decision Drivers' does not resolve. A listed driver is the leading token of a list item.
A requirement's non-empty traces_to.design names a design ID that does not exist. Fixed by hand in the requirements stage — there is no migration script and no bypass flag.
A requirement ID sits in traces_to.tests or traces_to.code, which hold test and code references. Fixed by hand in the requirements stage; the message names the exact edit.
A QA artifact's traces_from names an ID that exists in neither the requirements set nor the design set.
A functional requirement is cited by no component. Excludes priority: wont and status: obsolete.
An architecturally significant requirement is covered by no test strategy item. Excludes priority: wont and status: obsolete.
A listed decision driver resolves but is absent from that ADR's traces_from.
A requirement ID appears in the drivers prose but not as a list item, so it was never checked as a driver. A warning rather than an error: ordinary English mentioning an ID is history, not a defect.
A file's frontmatter did not parse, so it is missing from the index and the sweep was not complete.
Two files claim the same ID; only the last one read was indexed.

drivers.md is missing, unreadable, or has no '## Architecturally Significant Requirements' heading, so the ASR list came back empty and uncovered-asr could not fire this run — a clean uncovered-asr sweep does not mean every ASR is covered.
